question: On which Indian musician's life was the documentary film "Bansuri Guru" based on?
solution:
The correct answer is **Hari Prasad Chaurasia.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 2013 documentary film** Bansuri Guru is about the life of Indian classical musician Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia**
 
• He is a** renowned flute player and music director** in the Hindustani classical tradition.
 
• The** film covers key milestones in Chaurasia's life, including his childhood in Allahabad**,
 
 
• his time as an apprentice, and his work with All India Radio and in the Hindi film industry.
 
 
 
• **Rajeev Chaurasia**, the son of Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, directed the film.
 
• The title Bansuri Guru refers to the journey of mastering a passion and leaving a legacy for future generations
 
• He received **several awards, including the Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 1984, Padma Bhushan in 1992, and Padma Vibhushan in 2000.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **T. H. Vinayakram (Ghatam Maestro)**

 
 
• **He is ​**Renowned for playing the ghatam, a clay pot percussion instrument.
 
• He is a Master of Carnatic music, his ghatam playing is known for its precision and rhythm.
 
• Collaborated with international artists and part of the Grammy-winning group *Shakti*.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar (Sitar Maestro**)
 
 
• He Played a major role in popularising Indian classical music worldwide, especially in the West.
 
• He Worked with George Harrison of The Beatles, leading to a fusion of Indian and Western music.
 
• He is a Recipient of multiple prestigious awards, including three Grammy Awards and the Bharat Ratna.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma** (Santoor Maestro)
 
 
• He Revolutionized the *santoor*, a Kashmiri folk instrument, into an important instrument in Indian classical music.
 
• He is Known for his delicate yet powerful strokes and melodic nuances.
 
• He Collaborated with Hariprasad Chaurasia (flutist) as part of the Shiv-Hari duo to compose music for Bollywood films like Silsila and Chandni.
